comment: The only publication switch. Every Markdown file in the repository must match exactly one declaration. public entries name one file each, never a glob; internal entries may name a home and must state why the file stays in the repository.

internal.reason: standing orders for an agent editing this repository; the reader-facing rules live in README.md and docs/
product development plan: scope, architecture, milestones, and acceptance for contributors, not a user-facing guide
completed V0.1 (M0–M4) and V0.2 (M6–M12) development records, handoffs, and delivery results: environment- and version-bound historical evidence kept for audit, not current user guidance
PLAN V0.2 (plugin 0.2.0): M6–M12 staged plan and acceptance for the topic-session model rewrite; V0.1 remains in docs/PLAN.md as the M0–M4 record
decision records and their templates; internal history, not a guide
deferred and planned-away issue list for contributors: current status, ownership, and re-evaluation triggers; not a user-facing guide

Project-level AgentTeams rules: impact scanning, readiness as a task/event, fast contract tests before real E2E, one integration gate with bound artifact identity, executable reviewer policy, batched closeout, scoped E2E, delivery task and closeout metrics; internal guidance for captains and members, not a user-facing guide

Routing and topic-lifecycle diagrams for contributors: side-effect order, state ownership, and failure handling; the authoritative rules now live in src/routing.ts and src/route-tools.ts (sections 1-4 are the M4-era thread illustration kept for history), so this is internal review material rather than a published guide

Project-context illustration for contributors: the shared .dsh-cowork disk surface, memory injection timing, handoff up/down paths, and the four session isolation modes; the authoritative rules stay in src/ and docs/PLAN.md, so this route map is internal review material rather than a published guide
Cowork sidebar design docs and index: internal design drafts with background, design-process decisions, and demos; not user-facing until implementation lands
